questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. Climate change is no longer a distant warning—it is an unfolding reality with profound implications for life on Earth. Rising global temperatures, erratic weather patterns, melting glaciers, and frequent natural disasters signal a climate system in distress. What makes this crisis especially alarming is its scope: it threatens ecosystems, global economies, public health, food security, and geopolitical stability.Unlike other environmental concerns, climate change is not confined to a specific region or demographic. From island nations facing sea-level rise to agricultural heartlands enduring droughts, the effects are global and interconnected. Developing countries, despite contributing the least to greenhouse gas emissions, are often the most vulnerable, lacking the infrastructure to cope with such rapid changes.What elevates climate change to the level of an existential threat is its potential to trigger irreversible tipping points. These include the collapse of polar ice sheets, loss of biodiversity, and the disruption of ocean currents—all of which could accelerate warming beyond human control. Moreover, the resulting socio-political consequences—such as climate-induced migration, water conflicts, and food shortages—pose significant risks to peace and global governance.Addressing this crisis requires unprecedented international cooperation, rapid decarbonisation, and a fundamental shift in consumption patterns. Failure to act decisively may not just endanger future generations but jeopardise the survival of current ones. Climate change is not merely an environmental issue—it is a defining challenge for humanity’s continued existence.Which of the following is stated as a socio-political consequence of climate change?
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'D' (Climate-induced migration) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the following passages and answer the questions that follow.In today's global business environment, communication is often conducted in English, but cultural expectations can vary significantly. Misunderstanding cultural norms can lead to poor judgment and communication breakdowns. Three important areas where business etiquette differs across cultures include how people are addressed, the role of smiling, and expectations around eye contact.When addressing someone, different cultures have distinct preferences. For instance, a German professional may expect to be called 'Doctor' if they hold a PhD, valuing the title as recognition of effort and achievement. In contrast, a British person might find this overly formal or even pretentious. Continental Europeans and Latin Americans often prefer formal titles and surnames, while Americans and some British professionals lean towards using first names. The safest approach is to observe how others address you and ask if unsure.Smiling also carries different meanings. In Russia, it can be seen as insincere, while in countries like the United States, Britain, and Australia, it signals friendliness and respect. Research shows that smiling individuals are seen as more intelligent in some cultures such as Germany and China, but as less intelligent or even dishonest in places like Japan, Iran, and India.Eye contact is another area of divergence. In Western countries, it reflects attentiveness and honesty. However, in cultures such as Japan and Korea, it may be viewed as disrespectful. In parts of South America, Africa, and the Middle East, prolonged or cross-gender eye contact can be inappropriate or confrontational.Understanding these cultural nuances is important, but it is equally vital to avoid overgeneralising. Individuals are shaped by many factors beyond nationality, such as region, age, profession, and personal experience. Awareness without stereotyping is key to successful cross cultural communication.What is the central idea conveyed throughout the passage?
options: Business etiquette is the same across most countries.
Cultural sensitivity enhances international business communication.
English is the standard language for global business.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'C' (Cultural sensitivity enhances international business communication.) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.The room in which the boys were fed was a large stone hall, with a copper at one end, out of which the master ladled the gruel at mealtimes. Of this festive composition, each boy had one porringer, and no more—except on occasions of great public rejoicing, when he had two ounces and a quarter of bread besides. The bowls never wanted washing. The boys polished them with their spoons till they shone again; and when they had performed this operation (which never took long, the spoons being nearly as large as the bowls), they would sit staring at the copper with such eager eyes, as if they could have devoured the very bricks of which it was composed.  Oliver Twist and his companions suffered the tortures of slow starvation for three months. At last, they got so voracious and wild with hunger that one boy, taller than the rest, hinted darkly to his comrades that unless he had another basin of gruel, he might eat the weak boy next to him. A council was held; lots were cast to determine who should walk up to the master after supper to ask for more. The lot fell to Oliver.  Evening arrived; the boys took their places. The master, in his cook’s uniform, stationed himself at the copper. Oliver rose, trembling, and advancing to the master, said: “Please, sir, I want some more.” The master was a fat, healthy man, but he turned very pale. Staring in stupefied astonishment, he clung for support to the copper. The assistants were paralysed with wonder; the boys with fear. “What!” said the master at length, in a faint voice. “More?” The master then aimed a blow at Oliver's head with the ladle, pinioned him in his arms and shrieked aloud for the beadle.What did Oliver and the other boys have for their meals?

They had bowlfuls of nutritious meat soup every day, and on occasions, they were given eggs and a quarter of bread.
The boys had a bowl of gruel for regular meals, and on occasions, they were given two ounces of gruel and a quarter of bread.

questions.question: Comprehension:निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर पूछे गए प्रश्नों के उत्तर  दीजिए -देश-प्रेम है क्या? प्रेम ही तो है! बिना परिचय के प्रेम नहीं हो सकता। इस प्रेम का आलंबन क्या है? सारा देश अर्थात् मनुष्य, पशु-पक्षी, नदी-नाले, वन-पर्वत, सागर अर्थात् सारी भूमि और उसके सभी जीव – देश ही तो है! यह प्रेम किस प्रकार का है? यह साहचर्यगत प्रेम है। जिनके बीच हम रहते हैं. जिनका हमारा हर घड़ी का साथ रहता है, जिन्हें हम रोज आँखों से देखते हैं, जिनकी बातें हम रोज सुनते हैं अर्थात् जिनके सान्निध्य के हम अभ्यासी हो जाते हैं उनके प्रति राग या लोभ हो सकता है। पशु और बालक भी जिनके साथ अधिक रहते हैं, उनसे परच जाते हैं। यह परचना परिचय ही है और परिचय ही प्रेम का प्रवर्तक है। बिना परिचय के प्रेम नहीं हो सकता है। यदि प्रेम वास्तव में अंतःकरण का कोई भाव है तो देश के स्वरूप से परिचित और अभ्यस्त हो जाइए।बाहर निकलिए तो आँख खोलकर देखिए कि खेत कैसे लहलहा रहे हैं, नाले झाड़ियों के बीच कैसे बह रहे हैं, टेसू के फूलों से वनस्थली कैसी लाल हो रही है। कछारों में चौपायों के झुंड इधर-उधर चरते हैं, चरवाहे तान लड़ा रहे हैं, अमराइयों के बीच गाँव झाँक रहे हैं; उनमें घुसिए, देखिए तो क्या हो रहा है। जो मिले, उससे दो-दो बातें कीजिए, उनके साथ किसी पेड़ की छाया के नीचे घड़ी-आध-घड़ी बैठ जाइए इसलिए कि वे सब हमारे देश के हैं। इस प्रकार जब देश का रूप आपकी बुद्धि में समा जाएगा, आप उनके अंग-प्रत्यंग से परिचित हो जाएँगे, तब आपके अंतःकरण में इस इच्छा का सचमुच उदय होगा कि वह कभी न छूटे, वह सदा हरा-भरा और फला-फूला रहे, उसके धनधान्य की वृद्धि हो, उसके सभी प्राणी सुखी रहें।गद्यांश के अनुसार, देश-प्रेम किस प्रकार का भाव है?

questions.question: Comprehension:गद्यांश के आधार पर निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।इतिहास क्या है ? हमारा वर्तमान निरंतर अतीत में समाता जा रहा है। हम वर्तमान को देखते हैं। अतीत को हम नहीं देख पाते। लेकिन मनुष्य स्वभावतः इतिहास में भी निरंतर झांकने का प्रयास करता रहा है। अतीत में जाते रहने की प्रक्रिया में वर्तमान अपने कुछ चिह्न छोड़ जाता है। पुराने भवन, शिलालेख , ताम्रपत्र ,सिक्के ,भाषा ,साहित्य ,मिथक , किंवदंतियाँ आदि ऐसी ही चीजें हैं। इन्हें इतिहास का अवशेष समझना चाहिए। इन्हीं अवशेषों के आधार पर इतिहासकार इतिहास का पुनर्निर्माण करते हैं। आज अशोक नहीं है, किन्तु उसके शिलालेख हैं ; अकबर नहीं है, किन्तु आईने अकबरी है। इनसे जो जानकारियाँ मिलाती हैं, उन्हीं के आधार पर इतिहास की रचना होती है। ये अवशेष ही इतिहास की आधारभूत सामग्रियाँ हैं। साहित्य का इतिहास भी ऐसे ही पुनार्निर्मित किया जाता है। समस्त प्राचीन साहित्य जैसे चौरासी वैष्णवन की वार्ता , कबीर , सूर , तुलसी , जायसी ,मीरा , भारतेन्दु हरिश्चंद्र आदि की रचनाएँ हिंदी साहित्य के इतिहास लेखन की आधारभूत सामग्री हैं।गद्यांश में प्रयुक्त 'अतीत' का अर्थ कौन-सा नहीं  होगा ?

options: Reading, decoding words, and phonological processing
Performing basic arithmetic and algebraic calculations
Coordinating gross motor movements in outdoor sports
Expressing verbal emotions in social gatherings
questions.explanation: Dyslexia impairs a person's ability to read and comprehend text by affecting phonological awareness, spelling, and word recognition. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 17).

questions.question: [Test 24 - Q16] Inclusive Education in Indian classrooms fundamentally implies:
options: Educating children with special needs alongside non-disabled children in regular classrooms with appropriate adaptations
Establishing separate special schools for children with disabilities
Admitting only high-achieving gifted students in mainstream schools
Providing home-based schooling for all children with mild learning difficulties
questions.explanation: Inclusive education ensures that all children, regardless of their physical, cognitive, social, or linguistic abilities, learn together in the same mainstream educational environment. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 24).

questions.question: [Test 76 - Q11] Which quantitative method, developed by Jacob L. Moreno, is used to measure and map social relations, attractions, and repulsions within a classroom or group?
questions.explanation: Sociometry is a tool used to visually map and analyze social structures, peer acceptance, and interpersonal relationships within a classroom. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 76).

questions.question: [Test 1 - Q14] The term 'Hidden Curriculum' in educational sociology refers to:
options: Unwritten, unofficial, and unintended lessons, values, and perspectives that students learn in school
Secret syllabi taught only to select advanced students
Topics deleted from the official textbook by the examination board
Extracurricular sports activities held outside school hours
questions.explanation: The hidden curriculum consists of unspoken social norms, values, behaviors, and cultural expectations transmitted implicitly through the school environment. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 1).

questions.question: [Test 74 - Q5] In Benjamin Bloom's Mastery Learning model, what is the core assumption regarding student achievement?
options: Almost all students can master the material if provided with sufficient time and appropriate instruction
Intelligence is entirely fixed at birth and cannot be modified by pedagogical interventions
Only the top 10% of students are capable of high-order critical analysis
Written examinations should be designed to fail a high percentage of low-income pupils
questions.explanation: Mastery learning asserts that learning challenges are a function of instruction and time, rather than lack of student cognitive capacity. (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 74).

questions.question: [Test 40 - Q18] In Micro-Teaching, what is the standard ideal duration for a single micro-teaching cycle (Teach -> Feedback -> Re-plan -> Re-teach -> Re-feedback)?
questions.explanation: The standard NCERT micro-teaching cycle duration is 36 minutes: Teach (6m), Feedback (6m), Re-plan (12m), Re-teach (6m), Re-feedback (6m). (Question source: DSSSB Teaching Methodology Paper Series 40).
